findings.heading: ### B-1 CRITICAL (blocking) [Wiegers, Whittaker (sequence attack), Fowler]: Phase 1 ships `--unattended` on 37 commands while the behavior it promises arrives in P2-P4
findings.body:
Priority High. Quality impact: breaks the safety property of the whole contract for the interval between phases.

Grading sentence: An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds, in P1, an `--unattended` flag and `## Unattended mode` section on every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (S:159 "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (a no-op where a command has no gate)"; S:79; S:203 AC-1.1), while the gate and outward-default resolutions land only in P2 (S:160), P3 (S:161) and P4 (S:162). X is wrong because WC-2 (S:60) defines `--unattended` as "never calls AskUserQuestion, never ends its turn on a chat question" and WC-9 (S:67) turns every outward default off under it, and S:73 tells the coordinator to put `--unattended` in every brief "from Phase 1 on". After P1, `/sc:auggie-review <PR> --unattended` is accepted and still posts to GitHub by default (`cmd/auggie-review.md:51-54` via `INV-A:98`, UNVERIFIED directly; the row that fixes it is tagged P2, S:100), and `/sc:cleanup --unattended` still waits on its approval prompt (`INV-A:96`; row tagged P2, S:103). The "no-op" parenthesis at S:159 covers only commands without a gate, so the text does not say what the flag does on a command that has a gate before its phase. AC-1.1 (S:203) cannot detect it: it checks that a section exists and names `return-contract.yaml` and the contract path, not that the gate resolutions are present. S:154 ("each phase ... leaves standalone behaviour unchanged") says nothing about this window, and S:154 also says later phases do not start until earlier checks pass, so the window is the intended end state of P1.

State trace (Whittaker, FR-2.4 sequence attack): I can break this specification by **Sequence Attack**. The invariant at **S:60 / S:67** (under `--unattended` no prompt, no outward default) fails when **a coordinator follows S:73 after P1 merges but before P2**. Concrete attack: before, auggie-review has `--no-post-pr` default off and no `--unattended`; P1 adds `--unattended` as accepted-but-no-op; coordinator brief `/sc:auggie-review 123 --unattended --output d/`; after, the worker posts a PR review and ends its turn on the plain-chat remediation offer (`INV-A:62`), so there is an outward action and a silent stall with no `worker_done`, the exact failure the spec names as the real one (S:44).

Pipeline Dimensional Analysis (FR-19, a count mismatch is CRITICAL): N = 37 commands receive the flag in P1 (S:159); M = 15 have their gate behavior fixed at the end of P1 (9 P1 commands, S:159; plus adversarial, brainstorm, cleanup-audit, index-repo, init-lite, workflow, which are ready with the stated flags, S:81-92). 22 commands accept the flag with the gate unresolved: 11 needs-change plus 4 ready commands with small fixes in P2 (S:160), roadmap and save in P3 (S:161), and implement, post-release, pr-submit in P4 (S:162). Counts reconcile to 27 needs-change (9+11+4+3) and 10 ready.

Recommendation: add the flag and the `## Unattended mode` section to a command in the same phase that implements its gate and outward-default resolution (so P1 covers only the commands whose resolution is already complete), and rewrite S:7

findings.heading: ### F1. CRITICAL-to-blocking (graded MAJOR, blocking): acceptance check AC-1.1 cannot pass at the end of Phase 1
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers (testability, traceability), Adzic.
- Grading sentence: an implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a Phase 1 that is checked by AC-1.1 (every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`, and no section-4 command has one), and the check is wrong because the same document makes three of those commands impossible or out of phase at P1.
- Stated texts that contradict each other:
  1. AC-1.1 asserts the section on all of 3.1-3.2 (spec:203) and says a phase passes only when every check in its block passes (spec:167). Phase 1 scope says the `--unattended` flag is accepted by "every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2" (spec:159).
  2. The section 3.2 table assigns 17 of the 27 rows to P2, P3 or P4 (for example auggie-review P2 at spec:100, roadmap P3 at spec:118, implement P4 at spec:109, post-release P4 at spec:113, pr-submit P4 at spec:114), and says later phases do not start until the earlier phase passes (spec:154). Under that order a P1 pass needs the P2-P4 sections, but P4 waits on user decisions D2-D4 while "Phases 1-3 need no user decision" (spec:154, 233).
  3. `/sc:load` is in 3.2 with report "none", "use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task", and phase "P1 (usage line only)" (spec:112). The Decisions table says a report file would be an "unrequested addition" (spec:273). AC-1.1 would require it to have a section naming `return-contract.yaml`.
  4. Recommended D3(a) says pr-submit stays coordinator or person only, "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4" (spec:248). AC-1.1 would require pr-submit (a 3.2 row, spec:114) to carry the section, while section 4 says commands outside the worker set get none (spec:128).
- Wrong outcome: the P1 gate either fails permanently or forces an implementer to add contract sections to load and to a pr-submit the user has not agreed to make a worker, and to commands whose behaviour is still undecided.
- Recommendation (narrow, do not add): scope AC-1.1 and the P1 "flag accepted by" sentence to the commands the phase actually edits (the P1 command list at spec:159 plus the 3.1 ready rows), and state that load, and pr-submit under D3(a), carry no section. Each later phase's own check then asserts its commands.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: Testability 6 to 8.

findings.heading: ### F-01 (blocking, MAJOR, Wiegers, priority High)
findings.body:
- **Sentence.** An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds P1 so that every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 accepts `--unattended` and has a `## Unattended mode` section, because SPEC:159 and SPEC:195 say so; and the same implementer, following SPEC:94-125 and the P1 command list in the same SPEC:159 row, builds only 9 plus 6 of them, and AC-1.1 cannot pass for the other 22 until P2 to P4, which by SPEC:154 do not start until P1's checks pass.
- **Evidence.**
  - SPEC:159: P1 scope is "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2"; its command column lists only analyze, build, business-panel, design, document, explain, index, test, load, plus adversarial, cleanup-audit, index-repo, workflow, brainstorm and init-lite.
  - SPEC:160-162: auggie-review, cleanup, improve, cli-eval, cli-portify, recommend, research, review-translation, spec-panel, task, tasklist, reflect, release-split, tdd, troubleshoot are P2; roadmap, validate-roadmap, validate-tests, save are P3; implement, post-release, pr-submit are P4. The section 3.2 Phase column agrees (SPEC:99-125).
  - SPEC:195: AC-1.1 "asserts that every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`".
  - SPEC:154: "Later phases do not start until the earlier phase's checks in section 7 pass."

An implementer who resolves it toward the command list ships a P1 whose own acceptance test fails; one who resolves it toward AC-1.1 pulls 22 commands (including pr-submit, post-release and implement, which SPEC:162 holds for user decisions D2 to D4) into P1.

findings.heading: ### B-1  AC-1.1 cannot pass: it demands the `## Unattended mode` section in commands the spec itself assigns to later phases, leaves unchanged, or gives no contract
findings.body:
- **Severity**: CRITICAL, blocking. **Expert**: Wiegers (testability), with Whittaker (sequence attack) and Crispin (criterion coverage). **Priority**: High. **Quality-impact estimate**: Testability 8 to 4, Consistency 7 to 5 if left.
- **Stated texts that contradict**:
  1. `spec:205` (AC-1.1, a Phase 1 check): the test asserts "every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`". Sections 3.1 and 3.2 hold 37 commands (10 + 27).
  2. `spec:159` (Phase 1 scope) repeats the 37: "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2". Its command column lists only 12 (analyze, build, business-panel, design, document, explain, index, test, load, plus fixes to adversarial, cleanup-audit, index-repo).
  3. `spec:154` and `spec:162`: "Later phases do not start until the earlier phase's checks in section 7 pass" and Phase 4 (implement, post-release, pr-submit) "waits for answers to D2-D4".
  4. `spec:250`: under D3 option (a), the recommended one, "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4".
  5. `spec:84`, `spec:87`, `spec:92`: brainstorm, init-lite and workflow have small fix "None" and are not in any phase list. `spec:112`: `/sc:load` has "Report: none" and is to be used "as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task", so a section naming `return-contract.yaml` in `load` names a file it never writes.
- **Count mismatch (see Quantity Flow Diagram)**: the criterion covers 37 commands; the phases edit 34 in total, only 12 of them in Phase 1; 3 are never edited.
- **Grading sentence**: An implementer who follows AC-1.1 as written builds a Phase 1 that must add the section to implement, post-release and pr-submit (Phase 4, blocked on user decisions D2-D4 and, under D3 (a), not to be changed), to brainstorm, init-lite and workflow (rows say "None"), and to `load` (no contract), and X is wrong because the check can only pass if the implementer edits Phase 4 commands before the user decides, or edits commands the spec says to leave alone; otherwise Phase 1 never passes and, by `spec:154`, Phases 2-4 never start.
- **Recommendation** (narrow, do not add): restrict AC-1.1 and the Phase 1 sentence at `spec:159` to the commands that each phase's rows actually edit, and drop `load`, `brainstorm`, `init-lite` and `workflow` from the "names `return-contract.yaml`" assertion (or state the assertion per phase). Rationale: the per-row Phase column (`spec:83-125`) is already the authoritative assignment and is internally consistent; only the acceptance text over-reaches.

=== ARCHITECTURE ANALYSIS ===

No architecture finding reaches blocking grade. The decision itself (Orca coordinates, commands stay the units of work, `spec:13-39`) is consistent with the inventories: R1 to R5 each trace to a `CAPS` line that supports them (`CAPS:97-103`, `CAPS:145-150`, `INV-A:90`), and WC-7 and WC-8 do not depend on the unverified subagent questions (`spec:45`, `CAPS:159-160`). The architecture items below are Medium or minor.

findings.heading: ### F-02 (blocking, CRITICAL): Phase 1 scope and AC-1.1 cover 37 commands; the phase plan touches 13 and defers gates and outward defaults to P2-P4
findings.body:
Experts: Fowler (pipeline and count annotation), Whittaker (Divergence and Sequence attacks), Wiegers. Priority: High. Quality impact: Consistency +2, Testability +1. Labelled CRITICAL because Pipeline Dimensional Analysis classifies a count mismatch as CRITICAL (FR-19); it is blocking on its own consequence, shown below.

Where: SPEC:159 (P1 scope "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2"), SPEC:195 (AC-1.1), SPEC:99-125 (phase column), SPEC:160-162 (P2-P4), SPEC:154 and SPEC:225 (Phase 4 waits for D2-D4), SPEC:240 (D3(a)), SPEC:67 (WC-9), SPEC:73 (briefs carry `--unattended` from Phase 1), SPEC:112 (load writes no report).

Grading check: An implementer who follows the stated text as written adds `--unattended` and an `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` to all 37 commands of sections 3.1 and 3.2 in Phase 1 (SPEC:159, SPEC:195), including auggie-review, whose PR-posting default is switched off only in P2 (SPEC:100, SPEC:160), post-release and pr-submit, whose outward defaults wait for P4 and the user's answers (SPEC:113-114, 154, 162), and load, which writes no report (SPEC:112); X is wrong because SPEC:73 tells the coordinator to put `--unattended` in every brief from Phase 1, so a P1 `auggie-review` run accepts the flag and still posts to GitHub and offers remediation, which WC-9 (SPEC:67) and WC-2 (SPEC:60) say cannot happen under that flag, and because SPEC:154, SPEC:162 and D3(a) (SPEC:240, "no pr-submit changes") say P4 commands stay unchanged until the user decides. The other reading (13 commands, the P1 Commands column) makes AC-1.1 fail for the other 24, so the stated texts cannot both hold.

Concrete attack (Divergence, Sequence): before, P1 shipped, user runs the coordinator brief `/sc:auggie-review 123 --unattended --output d/` (SPEC:73 form). The flag is accepted (SPEC:159). Gate conversion is P2 (SPEC:100, 160), so the command posts the inline review comments and offers remediation (INV-A:38, SPEC:100); after: a GitHub write that the brief never authorized, plus a stall at the remediation offer with no `worker_done`.

Recommendation: narrow the P1 flag sentence and AC-1.1 to the commands P1 actually changes (the 13 in the Quantity Flow Diagram), delete the "every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2" wording, and say in section 2.3 that the brief carries `--unattended` only for a command whose phase has shipped. Do not add new mechanisms.

findings.heading: ### F-01 (CRITICAL, blocking) AC-1.1 cannot pass as written
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers (traceability), with Fowler (count flow) and Whittaker (divergence attack).
- Where: `SPEC:195` (AC-1.1) against `SPEC:112`, `SPEC:265`, `SPEC:159`, `SPEC:84`, `SPEC:87`, `SPEC:240`, `SPEC:154`.
- Grading sentence: an implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a P1 whose own acceptance test fails, and the test is wrong to fail only because the spec contradicts itself.
- The contradiction, with no further assumption:
  1. AC-1.1 passes only if "every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`" (`SPEC:195`). That is 37 commands.
  2. `/sc:load` is one of the 37 (`SPEC:112`). Its Report cell says "none (see note)", the note says to use it "as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task", and the Decisions table rejects a report file for it: "a report file would be an unrequested addition" (`SPEC:265`). A `load` section that names `return-contract.yaml` contradicts both.
  3. The phase table does not give two of the 37 to any phase: brainstorm (`SPEC:84`, fix "None") and init-lite (`SPEC:87`, fix "None") appear in no phase command list (`SPEC:158-162`). P1 does say the flag is "accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2" (`SPEC:159`), but P2 to P4 commands are the ones whose sections carry their gate resolutions (`SPEC:99-125`, phase column), and `SPEC:154` forbids starting a later phase until the earlier phase's checks pass.
  4. `/sc:pr-submit` is in the 37 (`SPEC:114`). The recommended decision D3(a) says "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4" and that the command is a worker candidate only if D3 is accepted otherwise (`SPEC:139-140`, `SPEC:240`). AC-1.1 still demands its section at P1.
- Concrete attack (Whittaker, divergence): P1 is done exactly as `SPEC:159` lists it (13 commands edited). `uv run pytest tests/skills/test_worker_contract.py` runs AC-1.1 and iterates over the 37. State trace before: 13 commands carry the section. After: the test finds 24 commands without it, among them `load`, for which the spec forbids a contract file. P1 cannot pass, so P2 to P4 never start (`SPEC:154`).
- Recommendation: narrow AC-1.1 to the commands each phase actually edits (the P1 list in `SPEC:159`), and say in the `load` row that it is exempt from the contract-section assertion. Do not add new commands to P1. Delete rather than add text where possible. Name a phase for brainstorm and init-lite or exempt them in the same sentence.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: restores the ability to pass P1 (Testability 4 to 7).

findings.heading: #### F-1. Phase 1 puts `--unattended` and an `## Unattended mode` section on every command, before the phases that make the flag safe
findings.body:
- Severity label: MAJOR. Grade: blocking. Experts: Wiegers (consistency), Nygard (what happens when the flag exists but the gate is not converted), Whittaker (sequence attack). Priority: High.
- Stated texts that collide:
  - P1 scope: "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (a no-op where a command has no gate)", and P1's rationale: "No person gate is involved, so each change is mechanical" (S:159).
  - AC-1.1, a P1 check: the test asserts "every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`, and that no section-4 command has one" (S:195).
  - Gate conversion is P2 (S:160), and P4 "waits for answers to D2-D4" and holds implement, post-release and pr-submit (S:154, S:162).
  - WC-9: "Under `--unattended`, any default that pushes, opens a PR, posts to GitHub ... is off" (S:67). WC-2: under `--unattended` the command never prompts (S:60).
  - Rows that contradict AC-1.1: load has "Report: none" and phase "P1 (usage line only)" (S:112); D3(a), the recommendation, says pr-submit gets "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4" and section 4 says pr-submit "stays a worker candidate only if the user accepts open decision D3" (S:240, S:139).
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows S:159 and S:195 as written adds `--unattended` plus a section that names `return-contract.yaml` to every command in 3.1 and 3.2 in Phase 1. That includes auggie-review, whose PR-posting default and remediation wait stay on until P2 (S:100, S:160; `INV-A:38`, `INV-A:78`), and implement, post-release and pr-submit, whose gates and outward actions wait for D2-D4 (S:162; `INV-B:33-34`). After P1 passes, those commands accept the flag that WC-9 and WC-2 say turns outward defaults and prompts off, while the defaults are still on. The wrong outcome is a coordinator that trusts the flag and gets a posted GitHub review, a push, or a stalled prompt (the silent stall of S:44). AC-1.1 also cannot pass for load (no contract file to name, S:112) and cannot pass together with D3(a), where pr-submit carries no unattended section.
- Quantity check (FR-19, see flow diagram): P1's flag scope names 37 commands (10 in 3.1 plus 27 in 3.2); P1's own command column names 13 (9 gate-free commands plus 4 fixes, S:159). The other 24 are changed in P2-P4 or not at all, so the "every command" count and the P1 command list diverge.
- Recommendation (narrow, do not add): limit P1's flag and section scope, and AC-1.1's quantifier, to the commands P1 lists; state that a command first accepts `--unattended` in the phase that converts its gates; drop load and pr-submit (while D3 is open) from AC-1.1's universal set.
- Quality impact: safety boundary (outward actions); blocks a correct Phase 1 acceptance run.

findings.heading: ### B3. Section 3.1 says ready commands change only in one column, which contradicts P1 and AC-1.1 (requirements)
findings.body:
- Evidence: `spec:79` says the ten ready commands "run as workers now" and "The only command changes are the small fixes in the last column." `spec:52` says each changed command "adds a short `## Unattended mode` section." P1 requires "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2" (`spec:159`). AC-1.1 requires every command in 3.1 to 3.2 to have the section (`spec:195`).
- Grading sentence: an implementer following `spec:79` leaves the ten ready commands without the `## Unattended mode` section and without the flag. AC-1.1 then fails in P1. The two stated texts contradict each other.
- Recommendation: change `spec:79` to say the ready commands also gain the section and the flag in P1, in addition to their small fixes.

findings.heading: ### B2. The ready tier (section 3.1) says no command changes, but section 2.3, P0, P1 and AC-1.1 require them
findings.body:
- **Sentence.** An implementer who follows section 3.1 ("These run as workers now", "The only command changes are the small fixes", spec:79) and runs the ten ready commands without `--unattended` builds workers that do not match section 2.3 (the brief must carry `--unattended`, spec:73) or the P0 check (spec:180 step 1 and spec:194, AC-0.4).
- P1 (spec:159) adds the `--unattended` flag to every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2. AC-1.1 (spec:195) requires every command in 3.1 and 3.2 to have a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml`. Section 3 says changed commands gain that section (spec:76). Brainstorm (spec:84) and init-lite (spec:87) list the small fix as "None", so AC-1.1 cannot pass for them as the tables are written.
- P0 is "no command edits" (spec:158), yet its smoke runs follow 7.2 (spec:194), and 7.2 needs the flag.
- **Expert.** Wiegers (traceability from section 2.3 to section 3.1); Fowler (interface drift between phase and table).
- **Recommendation.** Either give the ready tier the `--unattended` flag and section in P0 and say so in 3.1, or define P0 smoke runs without the flag and say which checks then apply.
- **Priority.** High. **Quality impact.** The phase gate for P0 and P1 cannot be run from the text.

findings.heading: ### F1 BLOCKING (CRITICAL, dimensional mismatch) Phase 1 gate asserts 37 commands, the plan assigns 9 to Phase 1
findings.body:
- Experts: Wiegers (traceability), Fowler (count annotation), Whittaker (divergence attack). Priority: High.
- Stated texts:
  - S:159 (P1 scope): "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2".
  - S:195 (AC-1.1): the test "asserts that every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`".
  - S:154 and S:167: "Later phases do not start until the earlier phase's checks in section 7 pass" and "A phase passes only when every check in its block ... passes".
  - Against it: the per-row Phase column puts implement (S:109), post-release (S:113) and pr-submit (S:114) in P4, and S:154 and S:162 say Phase 4 "waits for answers to D2-D4". D3(a), the recommendation, says "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4" (S:240). load has "Report: none" (S:112), so a section "naming `return-contract.yaml`" has nothing to name.
- Wrong outcome: An implementer who follows the stated text as written adds an `## Unattended mode` section (and the flag) to pr-submit, implement, post-release and the P2/P3 commands during Phase 1, or leaves them out and fails AC-1.1. The first reading edits the three commands whose design depends on user decisions that S:154 says are not yet answered, and contradicts D3(a). The second reading makes AC-1.1 unpassable, and because later phases may not start until it passes (S:154), Phases 2-4 never start. Both outcomes are wrong, and the cause is the two stated texts, not a guess.
- Count trace (see Quantity Flow Diagram): the 3.2 Phase column sums to 9 (P1) + 11 (P2) + 4 (P3) + 3 (P4) = 27; the P1 row names 9 commands from 3.2 plus fixes to 4 ready commands (S:159); AC-1.1 and the P1 flag sentence consume 37 (10 + 27).
- Recommendation: narrow AC-1.1 and the S:159 flag sentence to the commands the Phase column assigns to P1 (the nine named at S:159 plus the section 3.1 fixes), and state that a later phase adds the section for its own commands. Delete rather than add: no new mechanism is needed.
- Quality impact: Testability 3/10 for the rollout plan until fixed.

findings.heading: ### REQ-2 (MAJOR as labelled; graded BLOCKING) P1 and AC-1.1 require `--unattended` and its section on every command in 3.1/3.2, but the rows place the gate resolutions and WC-9 off-switches in P2 and P4
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers (phase traceability), Nygard (safety boundary between phases), Whittaker (sequence attack)
- Texts that contradict:
  - P1 scope (`spec:159`): "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (a no-op where a command has no gate)". AC-1.1 (`spec:195`): the test asserts every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`. Section 2.1 (`spec:52`): that section "lists only its own gate resolutions and report file".
  - Gate resolutions and outward-default switches are scheduled later: auggie-review P2 (`spec:100`), cli-eval P2 (`spec:104`), task P2 (`spec:121`), implement P4 (`spec:109`), post-release P4 (`spec:113`), pr-submit P4 (`spec:114`); P4 "waits for answers to D2-D4" (`spec:154,162`).
  - WC-9 (`spec:67`): "Under `--unattended`, any default that pushes, opens a PR, posts ... installs, provisions ... is off."
  - `/sc:load` (`spec:112`): report "none (see note)", "use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task"; AC-1.1 still requires its section to name `return-contract.yaml`.
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows P1 and AC-1.1 as written ships `--unattended` and a contract-naming section on auggie-review, post-release, pr-submit and task in P1, and the parenthesis "no-op where a command has no gate" does not cover them, so between P1 and P2/P4 `--unattended` is accepted while these commands still post to GitHub or run outward steps by default, and that is wrong because WC-9 says no outward default stays on under `--unattended` and the P4 commands are deliberately held until the user decides D2-D4; the same reading makes AC-1.1 demand a `return-contract.yaml` section for `/sc:load`, which section 3.2 says has no report.
- Recommendation: Narrow P1 and AC-1.1 to the commands whose rows are P1 (plus the ready commands needing no gate change), and have each later phase add the flag and section together with its gate resolutions. Exempt `/sc:load` from the contract-section assertion.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: avoids a half-wired flag that looks safe.

=== ARCHITECTURE ANALYSIS ===

No blocking architecture finding. The core decision holds: nesting depth 1 refuses a command that starts workers (`CAPS:97-99`, `spec:33`), Agent-tool subagents are outside that fence (`CAPS:155`, `spec:24`), `worker_done` is bound to the dispatched pane (`CAPS:76`, `spec:35`), and the six coordinator-only commands match both inventories (`INV-A:87-92`, `INV-B:282-287`, `spec:130-137`). The Medium items below are listed under follow-up candidates.

=== ADVERSARIAL ANALYSIS (Whittaker) ===

Attack results: sequence attack produced REQ-2; divergence attack on the contract path produced REQ-1. Remaining attacks produced Medium items only (M-3, M-5, M-6 below). Sentinel collision: `partial` maps to `succeeded` (`spec:63,263`), so a coordinator that keys on `--outcome` alone cannot tell a partial run from a full one; the spec covers this with the body's first sentence and the contract (WC-5), so it is OK.

findings.heading: ### F2 (CRITICAL, blocking): AC-1.1 and the P1 scope contradict the rows they test
findings.body:
Experts: Wiegers (traceability), Crispin (an acceptance check that cannot pass), Cockburn (who gets the mode).
Stated texts:
- AC-1.1, `:195`: the test "asserts that every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`". P1 scope, `:159`: "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2".
- `:76`: "Every changed command also gains the `## Unattended mode` section", and `:79`: for the ready commands "The only command changes are the small fixes in the last column", where brainstorm and init-lite have "None" (`:84`, `:87`).
- `/sc:load`, `:112`: report "none (see note)", "use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task"; Decisions, `:265`: "a report file would be an unrequested addition. Only its usage-line defect is fixed."
- implement, post-release and pr-submit are phase P4 (`:114`, `:113`, `:109`), and `:154-155`, `:162` say "Phase 4 waits for answers to D2-D4"; D3 option (a), recommended, says "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4" (`:240`), and section 4 says `/sc:pr-submit` stays a worker candidate "only if the user accepts open decision D3" (`:139`).

Sentence: An implementer who follows the stated text as written writes the P1 test of AC-1.1 and gets a test that fails for brainstorm, init-lite and load unless each gains a section that names `return-contract.yaml` (adding a contract to load that `:265` forbids, and a change to init-lite and brainstorm that `:79` rules out), and that forces an `--unattended` section into implement, post-release and pr-submit in P1 although their gate and outward-action decisions D2-D4 are not made until P4 and D3 (a) says pr-submit gets no change. This is wrong because an acceptance check and the rows it tests state opposite scopes, so no change set satisfies both and P1 cannot be declared passed (`:154` "Later phases do not start until the earlier phase's checks pass").

findings.heading: ### F-01 (blocking, MAJOR) Phase 1 scope states two different sets of commands, and AC-1.1 cannot pass against the smaller one
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers (traceability), Adzic (example), Whittaker (FR-2.2 divergence attack and FR-19 count mismatch).
- Locations: SPEC:159 (P1 row), SPEC:195 (AC-1.1), SPEC:52 (what each command section contains), SPEC:160-161 (P2 and P3 rows).
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds Phase 1 for the 13 commands in the P1 "Commands" cell (9 from section 3.2 plus adversarial, cleanup-audit, index-repo, workflow; 12 once `/sc:load` is excluded), and that is wrong because AC-1.1 requires a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md` on every command whose row is phased P1 to P3 except load, which is 31 commands, so the Phase 1 gate in section 7 cannot pass. The other reading (the P1 "Scope" sentence at SPEC:159, "every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 that section 3 assigns to a phase") builds the section on 31 commands in Phase 1, and that is wrong because SPEC:52 says each section lists the command's gate resolutions, which SPEC:160-161 assign to Phases 2 and 3, and SPEC:154 says a later phase does not start until the earlier phase's checks pass.
- Concrete count trace: P1 "Commands" cell = 13 (12 without load). AC-1.1 set = 13 + 15 (P2) + 4 (P3) - 1 (load) = 31. Difference = 19 commands (the 15 P2 and 4 P3 commands). See the Quantity Flow Diagram.
- Recommendation: state one set. Delete the AC-1.1 reference to P2 and P3 commands (assert only the P1 commands), or move the section and flag for P2 and P3 commands out of the P1 scope sentence. Narrow, do not add.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: Testability and Consistency each drop about 2 of 10 until fixed.

findings.heading: **F1. BLOCKING. CRITICAL. Expert: Wiegers (lead), Adzic. Priority: High. Quality impact: Phase 1 cannot pass its own acceptance check.**
findings.body:
Issue: Three texts disagree about what Phase 1 changes.
- Phase 1 scope says the `--unattended` flag is "accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (a no-op where a command has no gate)" (`S:159`).
- The Phase 1 Commands column lists only analyze, build, business-panel, design, document, explain, index, test, load (usage line only), plus fixes to adversarial, cleanup-audit, index-repo and workflow (`S:159`). That is 12 commands.
- AC-1.1 asserts that every command in sections 3.1-3.2 except `/sc:load` has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md` (`S:202`). That is 36 commands (10 + 27 - 1).

The same sections are assigned elsewhere to later phases:
- The gate resolutions for 15 commands belong to Phase 2 (`S:160`).
- Four commands belong to Phase 3 (`S:161`).
- implement, post-release and pr-submit belong to Phase 4, which "waits for D2-D4" (`S:154`, `S:162`, `S:109`, `S:113`, `S:114`).

Section 2.1 says each section "lists only its own gate resolutions" (`S:52`). So AC-1.1 requires Phase 1 to write sections whose gate resolutions the spec defers to Phase 2-4, and for Phase 4 to the undecided D2-D4.

Concrete wrong outcome: An implementer who follows the Phase 1 Commands column builds 12 command edits. AC-1.1 then fails for the other 24 commands, so Phase 1 cannot pass (`S:167`, "A phase passes only when every check in its block ... passes"). An implementer who follows AC-1.1 writes `## Unattended mode` sections for implement, post-release and pr-submit before D2-D4 are answered. Those commands would then accept `--unattended` while their gates still wait, which is exactly the stall WC-2 forbids (`S:60`). Phase 1 live checks (AC-1.2) cover only "each P1 command" (`S:203`), so no check catches that stall.

Recommendation (for the reviser, narrow): restrict AC-1.1 and the Phase 1 scope sentence to the Phase 1 command list, and give each later phase its own "section exists" assertion alongside its gate assertions (AC-2.1 already has the pattern, `S:207`). Do not add a new mechanism.

findings.heading: ### B-2 | MAJOR (blocking) | Wiegers, Cockburn | priority High | quality impact: Completeness -1, Testability -1
findings.body:
**Issue.** Section 3.1 says the ten ready commands report "the named file until Phase 1 adds the contract" (spec:79), and the init-lite row names a contract "in the parent directory of that file" (spec:87). The phase table gives P1 only nine commands plus "fixes to adversarial, cleanup-audit, index-repo, workflow" (spec:159), P2 fifteen commands (spec:160), P3 four (spec:161) and P4 three (spec:162). Count: 13 + 15 + 4 + 3 = 35 of the 37 worker-capable commands. Brainstorm (spec:84, small fix "None") and init-lite (spec:87, small fix "None") appear in no phase's Commands column. Section 6 says each phase "adds the flag and the section for its own commands" (spec:159), AC-1.1 asserts the section only for P1 commands (spec:195), and section 2.3 requires the brief to include `--unattended` (spec:73).

**Grading sentence.** An implementer who follows section 6 as written completes P0 to P4 and delivers no `## Unattended mode` section, no `--unattended` flag handling and, for init-lite, no `return-contract.yaml` at all; this is wrong because section 3.1 and section 2.3 tell the coordinator to brief those two commands with `--unattended` and to open a contract at a computed path, and the spec's acceptance checks (AC-1.1, AC-1.2) never test either command, so every check passes while the stated contract does not exist. The 3.1 lead-in sentence and the section 6 table contradict.

**Recommendation.** Assign brainstorm and init-lite to a phase (P1 is the natural one: no gate), or state in the 3.1 rows that they need no change and the brief must not pass `--unattended` to them. Cite this finding id on whichever line is added.

findings.heading: ### B-1 (Wiegers, Crispin, Fowler): AC-1.1 cannot pass against the spec's own Phase 1 scope
findings.body:
Sentence: An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a Phase 1 that touches 13 commands (S:159 lists analyze, build, business-panel, design, document, explain, index, test, load, plus fixes to adversarial, cleanup-audit, index-repo, workflow), and that is wrong because AC-1.1 (S:195) asserts that every one of the 37 commands in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml`, so the phase's own pass condition fails for 24 commands, and S:154 ("Later phases do not start until the earlier phase's checks pass") then blocks P2-P4.

Evidence, all in S:
- S:159: P1 scope is "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2" but its command list names 13.
- S:79: ready commands get "only ... the small fixes in the last column"; brainstorm (S:84) and init-lite (S:87) say "None", and neither is in the P1 list (S:159).
- S:112 and S:265: `load` writes no report and "a report file would be an unrequested addition", yet AC-1.1 requires its section to name `return-contract.yaml`.
- S:139 and S:240-242: `pr-submit` is a worker candidate only if D3 is accepted; the recommended D3(a) says "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4". S:114 and S:162 assign pr-submit's contract and gate resolutions to P4. AC-1.1 forces a pr-submit section naming `return-contract.yaml` in P1, before D3 is answered. S:154 and S:225 say P1-P3 need no user decision and proceed on the recommendations.
- P2 and P4 gate resolutions are defined per command (S:100-125) and scheduled later (S:160, S:162), so a P1 section for those commands cannot yet carry them.
- Count trace: expected sections 37 (S:195) versus commands in P1 scope 13 (S:159) versus ready-no-change rows 2 (brainstorm, init-lite).

findings.heading: ### B-1 (blocking, CRITICAL). The Phase 1 acceptance check AC-1.1 cannot pass as scoped, and two ready commands sit in no phase
findings.body:
Experts: Wiegers (traceability), Fowler (count annotation, Pipeline Dimensional Analysis).

Grading check. An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds Phase 1 as the row at SPEC:159 lists it (nine no-gate commands plus fixes to adversarial, cleanup-audit, index-repo, workflow), and then runs AC-1.1 (SPEC:195), which asserts that every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml`. That is wrong because AC-1.1 cannot pass: 37 commands are asserted, and these are among them although Phase 1 does not give them the section or cannot give it one:

- `/sc:load` gets no report file at all (SPEC:112, "Report: none", "use it as a step inside another worker's brief"), so its section cannot name `return-contract.yaml`.
- `/sc:pr-submit` is Phase 4 (SPEC:114, 162), and D3 option (a), the recommendation, says "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4" (SPEC:240) while "Phases 0-3 can proceed on the recommendations" (SPEC:225).
- The Phase 2, 3 and 4 commands (SPEC:160-162) are not edited in Phase 1.
- `/sc:brainstorm` and `/sc:init-lite` appear in section 3.1 with "Small fix: None" (SPEC:84, 87) and in no phase row (SPEC:158-162), yet AC-1.1 asserts they carry the section.

SPEC:154 ("Later phases do not start until the earlier phase's checks in section 7 pass") then stops Phase 2 from starting. The sentence at SPEC:159 ("the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2") and the command list in the same row (SPEC:159) also disagree, so no reading makes AC-1.1 and the phase table both true.

Quantity Flow Diagram (Pipeline Dimensional Analysis, triggered by the 43 -> classification -> phase flow; FR-19 mismatch):

```text
[Inventories: 21 (INV-A:3) + 22 (INV-B:3)] --> [43 commands, SPEC:76]
   |--> [3.1 ready: 10, SPEC:81-92]  --> P1 fixes 4 (adversarial, cleanup-audit, index-repo, workflow; SPEC:159)
   |                                 --> P2 4 (reflect, release-split, tdd, troubleshoot; SPEC:160)
   |                                 --> NO PHASE 2 (brainstorm SPEC:84, init-lite SPEC:87)  <-- MISMATCH 10 in, 8 out
   |--> [3.2 needs change: 27, SPEC:97-125] --> P1 9 + P2 11 + P3 4 + P4 3 = 27 (consistent)
   |--> [section 4: 6, SPEC:130-137] (no mode, SPEC:128)
[AC-1.1 consumer, SPEC:195: expects section in 37 commands at the end of P1]  <-- MISMATCH vs at most 13 edited in P1 (9 + 4)
```

Recommendation and rationale. Narrow AC-1.1 so it asserts only the commands that the Phase column assigns to the phase being checked or an earlier one, excluding `/sc:load` (no contract) and `/sc:pr-submit` until D3 is answered, and give `brainstorm` and `init-lite` a phase (or state that they receive the section in P1). Narrowing removes the deadlock without adding a mechanism. Priority: High. Quality impact: Testability +2.

findings.heading: ### B-2 (CRITICAL, blocking) Phase 1 gives every worker command the `--unattended` section before the phases that convert their gates
findings.body:
Experts: Fowler (lead, count annotation), Whittaker (Divergence Attack), Nygard.

Location: spec:159 (P1 scope "accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 except the P4 commands"), spec:195 (AC-1.1), spec:100 (auggie-review row, Phase P2), spec:118 (roadmap row, P3), spec:160 (P2), INV-A:38, INV-A:78.

Grading sentence: An implementer who follows P1 and AC-1.1 as written makes `/sc:auggie-review` accept `--unattended` and write a section naming `return-contract.yaml` and the contract path, while its gate conversion (`--no-post-pr`, `--no-remediation-offer`) is a P2 row, so after P1 `/sc:auggie-review <PR> --unattended` still posts a review and inline comments to GitHub with no prompt (INV-A:38) and then waits on a remediation offer, which is the outward action and the stall that WC-2 and WC-9 say the flag removes, and AC-1.1 passes.

I can break this specification by **Divergence Attack**. The invariant at **spec:159 / spec:195** fails when **a gated command's phase (P2 or P3 in its own row) is later than the phase that adds its `--unattended` flag (P1)**. Concrete attack: P1 merged, P2 not yet. The coordinator's brief template (P0) says `--unattended` implies no person and no outward default; it runs `/sc:auggie-review 123 --unattended --output d/`; the command posts to PR 123 and ends its turn on the remediation offer; no `worker_done` arrives. The same applies to `roadmap` (the "Resume? [Y/n]" prompt stays until P3), `cli-eval`, `cli-portify`, `task`, `cleanup`, `improve` and the other 11 P2 / P3 commands in 3.2. Count: AC-1.1 requires 33 commands to hold the section after P1; the P1 command column lists 12 (see the Quantity Flow Diagram).

The spec already sees the hazard for P4 and fixes it there (spec:159 and spec:195, "F-2": those commands get the flag in P4). The same reason applies to every command whose gate row is not P1.

Recommendation (narrowing): in P1 and AC-1.1, give each command its `## Unattended mode` section and flag in the phase named in its own section 3 row, as already done for the P4 commands.

findings.heading: ### B3 - Phase 1 ships `--unattended` and the "Unattended mode" section on commands whose gate resolutions, GitHub-post-off default and decisions arrive only in P2 and P4
findings.body:
- Severity: CRITICAL. Experts: Fowler (lead), Newman (versioning/sequence), Nygard. Priority: High. Quality impact: Consistency -2, safety.
- Location: `spec:159` (P1 scope), `spec:195` (AC-1.1), `spec:76` (section 3 intro), `spec:73` (section 2.3), `spec:67` (WC-9), `spec:100` (auggie-review row), `spec:160` and `spec:162` (P2, P4), `spec:241` and `spec:240` (D3), `spec:154` and `spec:225`.
- Grading check: an implementer who follows P1 and AC-1.1 as written builds `--unattended` plus an `## Unattended mode` section naming only `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md` on every command of sections 3.1 and 3.2, including auggie-review, cli-portify, implement, post-release and pr-submit, "a no-op where a command has no gate" (`spec:159`). That is wrong because section 2.3 tells the coordinator to put `--unattended` in the brief "from P1 on" (`spec:73`) and WC-9 says that under `--unattended` the GitHub-posting default is off (`spec:67`); until P2 lands, `/sc:auggie-review <PR> --unattended` still posts a PR review with no prompt (`INV-A:38`). For pr-submit the P1 section also contradicts D3(a), "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4" (`spec:240`), because the command would carry an unattended contract before the user decides whether it is a worker at all.
- Divergence attack (Whittaker): the boundary between P1 and P2 is a state where the flag exists and its documented meaning (WC-2, WC-9) is false for 15 commands.
- Recommendation: add the flag and the section to a command in the same phase that implements its gate resolution (or have AC-1.1 cover only the P1 commands and the 3.1 ready commands); state that `--unattended` on a not-yet-converted command is refused, not ignored.

=== ARCHITECTURE ANALYSIS ===

No architecture finding reaches blocking. The central decision (Orca on top, commands stay units of work, `spec:13-45`) is supported: the rejected alternative rests on checkable facts (`CAPS:97-103`, `CAPS:147-150`, `CAPS:145`, `INV-A:90`, `INV-B:285-286`), and the spec states the weak points plainly (`spec:41-45`). Fowler/Newman/Hohpe/Nygard notes on interfaces and sequencing are in the Medium list below (M4, M5, M7, M13, M15).

findings.heading: ### B1 (MAJOR, blocking, Fowler / Wiegers): Phase 1 ships `--unattended` on every command, while the gate and outward-action rules that give the flag its meaning arrive in P2 to P4
findings.body:
Quoted texts:
- S:159 (P1): "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (a no-op where a command has no gate)".
- S:195 (AC-1.1): the test "asserts that every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`".
- S:60 (WC-2): "Under `--unattended` the command never calls `AskUserQuestion`, never ends its turn on a chat question ...".
- S:67 (WC-9): "Under `--unattended`, any default that pushes ... posts to GitHub ... is off."
- S:100, S:103, S:160: auggie-review's posting-off, cleanup's approval handling and every gate conversion are P2 (S:160: "These changes touch no safety rule ... P2 only turns it off under `--unattended`").

An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds, at the end of P1, an `auggie-review` and a `cleanup` that accept `--unattended`, carry the section AC-1.1 demands, pass AC-1.1, and still post to the PR and still prompt. That is wrong because WC-2 and WC-9 define `--unattended` as never prompting and never acting outward, and the "no-op where a command has no gate" parenthesis does not cover these commands, which do have gates. The coordinator brief (S:73) is told to pass `--unattended` on every worker, so a P1-only install would post PR reviews on a fork PR and stall silently, the failure mode the spec was written to remove (S:44, point 2). The sequencing statement at S:154 ("Phases 1-3 need no user decision") does not resolve it: nothing says gated commands refuse or ignore the flag until their phase.

Reviser brief note: narrow P1 and AC-1.1 to the commands whose rows say "no gate" (and the section-3.1 commands whose row needs no gate conversion), and state that a gated command does not gain `--unattended` before its own phase.

findings.heading: ### F-02 [MAJOR, blocking] P1 scope and AC-1.1 / AC-1.2 contradict the rest of the plan and leave `--unattended` unsafe between phases
findings.body:
- Experts: Fowler, Nygard, Whittaker (Sequence attack). Priority High. Quality impact: Consistency -3, safety posture of the interim state.
- Grading sentence: an implementer who follows the stated text builds P1 so that `--unattended` is "accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (a no-op where a command has no gate)" (spec:159) and so that AC-1.1 (spec:195) finds a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` in all 37 commands, while the gate conversions that make the flag safe arrive in P2 to P4 (spec:160-162); at the end of P1, `/sc:auggie-review <PR> --unattended` still posts to the PR and offers remediation (spec:100, INV-A:38), `/sc:task` still commits and pushes on EXEMPT keywords (spec:121), and `/sc:post-release` still installs and provisions (spec:113), which WC-2 and WC-9 (spec:60, 67) say never happens under `--unattended`; the plan says every phase is independently useful (spec:154).
- Contradictions inside the same scope, each a stated text:
  - 3.1 intro: "The only command changes are the small fixes in the last column" (spec:79), and brainstorm and init-lite say "None" (spec:84, 87) and appear in no phase (section 6, spec:159-162); AC-1.1 requires them to gain a section.
  - load: report "none", "use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task" (spec:112, 265); AC-1.1 requires it to name `return-contract.yaml`, and AC-1.2 runs it with `--unattended --output <dir>` (spec:196).
  - AC-1.2 runs every P1 command with `--output <dir>` (spec:196), but index-repo, cleanup-audit and workflow have no such flag in their rows (spec:85, 86, 92).
  - pr-submit, implement and post-release are listed in AC-1.1's set, yet "Phases 1-3 need no user decision" (spec:154) and P4 waits on D2-D4 (spec:162); under D3 option (a) the recommended outcome is "no pr-submit changes" (spec:240).
- Recommendation: restrict the `--unattended` flag, its section and its AC-1.x checks to the commands the phase converts (the P1 list in spec:159, using the section 6 command list), and add that a command accepts `--unattended` only in the phase that resolves its gates. Rationale: it deletes scope instead of adding rules and removes the unsafe interim state.

findings.heading: ### F2. MAJOR, blocking. Section 3.1 says ready commands change only by their small fix; Phase 1 and AC-1.1 add `--unattended` and an `## Unattended mode` section to every one of them
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers.
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows SPEC:79 ("The only command changes are the small fixes in the last column") leaves `brainstorm` and `init-lite` (small fix "None", SPEC:84, SPEC:87) unedited, and is then wrong because SPEC:159 requires "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2", SPEC:76 gives every changed command the section, and AC-1.1 (SPEC:195) asserts the section for every command in 3.1-3.2, so the test fails on those two commands (and on other "None" or already-contracted rows).
- Evidence: SPEC:76, SPEC:79, SPEC:84, SPEC:87, SPEC:159, SPEC:195; SPEC:79 also says the worker reports the named file "until Phase 1 adds the contract", but brainstorm already writes `<output>/return-contract.yaml` (SPEC:84; INV-A:39).
- Recommendation: replace the second sentence at SPEC:79 with "Phase 1 also adds `--unattended` and the `## Unattended mode` section to each of these commands." (an added sentence replacing a contradicted one), or restrict AC-1.1 to the commands that have a small fix.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: Consistency 6 to 8.

findings.heading: ### B-1 (BLOCKING): section 3 says ready commands change only by their small fixes, but P1 and AC-1.1 require every one of them to change
findings.body:
- Issue: `spec:79` says "The only command changes are the small fixes in the last column" for the ten ready commands. `spec:159` (P1) requires the `--unattended` flag "accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2", and `spec:195` (AC-1.1) requires a `## Unattended mode` section in every 3.1 command. Brainstorm (`spec:84`) and init-lite (`spec:87`) have no fix, so an implementer following `spec:79` leaves them untouched and fails P1 and AC-1.1. Following P1 and AC-1.1 adds a change that `spec:79` denies.
- Sentence: "An implementer who follows `spec:79` leaves brainstorm and init-lite unchanged, and that is wrong because `spec:195` requires them to carry a `## Unattended mode` section."
- Severity: MAJOR, blocking (two stated texts contradict).
- Expert: Wiegers (traceability), Cockburn.
- Recommendation: state one rule. Either every 3.1 command gets the flag and section (and `spec:79` is rewritten to say so), or AC-1.1 and P1 exclude commands whose only change is "none". Name the set explicitly.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: high (a test that cannot be made to pass as written).

findings.heading: ### F2. Two commands needing a change are assigned to no phase, so AC-1.1 cannot pass. BLOCKING. CRITICAL.
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers (lead), Fowler (count check).
- Issue: `brainstorm` (`spec:84`) and `init-lite` (`spec:87`) are in section 3.1 and need the `## Unattended mode` section. The phase rows (`spec:159-162`) list P1 13 commands, P2 15, P3 4, P4 3, for 35 in total. The 3.1 and 3.2 rows add up to 37 (10 + 27). Neither brainstorm nor init-lite appears in any phase row. P1 says the flag is accepted "by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2" (`spec:159`), and AC-1.1 asserts the section for every such command (`spec:195`).
- Grading check: An implementer who follows the phase table builds 35 of the 37 changes and leaves brainstorm and init-lite without `--unattended`, and that is wrong because `spec:195` requires the section for every command in 3.1-3.2.
- Recommendation: Add brainstorm and init-lite to P1. init-lite also needs the F4 fix.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: AC-1.1 fails in P1 and in every later phase; see also the Pipeline Dimensional Analysis below.

findings.heading: ### B-4 (BLOCKING). Section 3.1 says ready commands change only by small fixes; P1 and AC-1.1 require more
findings.body:
- Expert: Karl Wiegers (lead). Severity: MAJOR, blocking (two stated texts contradict).
- Location: candidate:79 ("The only command changes are the small fixes in the last column"); candidate:76 ("Every changed command also gains the `## Unattended mode` section"); candidate:84 (brainstorm, fix "None") and candidate:87 (init-lite, fix "None"); candidate:159 (P1 scope: "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 ... The WC-4 contract in unattended mode"); candidate:195 (AC-1.1 asserts a `## Unattended mode` section in every command in sections 3.1-3.2).
- Issue: a reader who follows candidate:79 leaves brainstorm and init-lite unchanged, so they have no flag and no section. AC-1.1 then fails for those two. P1 also says the flag must be accepted by all 3.1 commands. In addition, the phase table's Commands column (candidate:158-162) lists neither brainstorm nor init-lite, so no phase owns them, and reflect, release-split, tdd and troubleshoot (ready today) sit in P2.
- Grading check: "An implementer who follows the 3.1 introduction leaves brainstorm and init-lite without a `## Unattended mode` section and without the flag, and AC-1.1 then fails for those two, because AC-1.1 requires the section for every command in 3.1."
- Recommendation: rewrite candidate:79 to say every ready command gains the flag and section (a no-op where there is no gate), and list brainstorm and init-lite in a phase's Commands column.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: P1 completion is ambiguous for two of ten ready commands.

findings.heading: ### B3. Section 3.1 says the ready commands change only in the last column, but P1 and AC-1.1 require the flag on all of them
findings.body:
- Expert: Fowler (change scope), Wiegers (consistency). Severity: MAJOR, graded blocking because two stated texts contradict each other.
- Location: spec:79 ("The only command changes are the small fixes in the last column"), spec:84 (brainstorm, fix "None"), spec:87 (init-lite, fix "None"), spec:159 (P1: "the --unattended flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2"), spec:195 (AC-1.1).
- Issue: Brainstorm and init-lite have no change under spec:79, so an implementer following it adds no flag and no Unattended section to either. AC-1.1 requires the section in every 3.1 command, and P1 requires the flag.
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows spec:79 leaves brainstorm and init-lite without `--unattended`, then AC-1.1 fails for both; X is wrong because P1 requires the flag on every 3.1 command, so the spec contradicts itself on the scope of change.
- Recommendation: Rewrite spec:79 to say that P1 adds `--unattended`, the Unattended section and the WC-4 contract to all ten 3.1 commands, and state the minimal change for brainstorm and init-lite.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: scope of change is misstated for 10 commands.

findings.heading: ### B1 [CRITICAL, blocking] AC-1.1 and the P1 scope require unattended mode in the three commands whose behavior is deferred to the user's decisions
findings.body:
- Where: SPEC:159 (P1 "flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2"), SPEC:195 (AC-1.1 "every command in sections 3.1-3.2 except `load` has a `## Unattended mode` section ... and no section-4 command has one"), against SPEC:154 ("Phase 4 waits for answers to D2-D4"), SPEC:162 (P4 = implement, post-release, pr-submit), SPEC:109,113,114 (their gate resolutions depend on D2/D4/D3), SPEC:128 and SPEC:139 (pr-submit "stays a worker candidate only if the user accepts D3"), SPEC:240 (D3(a), recommended: "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4").
- Grading check (PROMPTS:31): An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds, in Phase 1, a `## Unattended mode` section and an accepted `--unattended` flag in `implement`, `post-release` and `pr-submit` (to pass AC-1.1), and that is wrong because SPEC:154 and SPEC:162 make those three behaviors wait for D2-D4, SPEC:240 says the recommended D3 gives pr-submit no changes, and SPEC:128 says a command that is not a worker gets no unattended mode. Two stated texts contradict each other and AC-1.1 cannot be satisfied together with SPEC:162 and SPEC:240.
- Expert: Wiegers (consistency of requirements), Fowler (phase boundary), Whittaker (Sequence Attack): I can break this specification by **Sequence Attack**. The invariant at **SPEC:154-162** (user decisions precede the three safety-relevant commands) fails when **P1 is executed to pass AC-1.1**. Concrete attack: Before P1, `cmd/pr-submit.md` has no unattended mode (SPEC:25 baseline). P1 adds a section naming `return-contract.yaml` (SPEC:195). The user then picks D3(a). After P1, pr-submit ships an unattended mode that SPEC:240 says should not exist.
- Recommendation: narrow AC-1.1 and the P1 scope sentence to the commands outside P4 (the 33), and let the P4 phase add the three sections after D2-D4. Rationale: it deletes a clause rather than adding a mechanism, and it restores the order SPEC:154 already states.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: Consistency +2, Testability +1.

findings.heading: ### F-02 (Blocking, label MAJOR; Wiegers, Cockburn) `/sc:load` is listed both ways, and the P1 acceptance checks select it
findings.body:
Where: `spec:112` (load row), `spec:159` (P1 scope), `spec:76` (every changed command gains the section), `spec:195` (AC-1.1), `spec:196` (AC-1.2), `spec:183` (7.2 step 4).

Grading check: An implementer who follows spec:159 builds, for every P1 command named there, the `--unattended` flag and `## Unattended mode` section; spec:159 names `load (usage line only)` in that list, and spec:76 says every changed command gains the section. AC-1.1 then asserts that "every command whose section 3 phase is P1" has a section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md` (spec:195), and AC-1.2 runs 7.2 on "each P1 command with `--unattended --output <dir>`" (spec:196), which requires a contract file that parses with `status` and `command` (spec:183). But the load row says Report: "none", Resume "n/a", and "use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task" (spec:112), and the Decisions table says a report file "would be an unrequested addition" (spec:265). Following the load row fails AC-1.1 and AC-1.2; following the AC adds a contract that spec:265 rejects. The same selector problem catches adversarial, cleanup-audit and index-repo, whose 3.1 rows carry "(P1)" for a small fix only (spec:83, spec:85, spec:86), while spec:159 gives them no `--unattended` section. Two stated texts contradict each other.

Recommendation (rationale: remove the contradiction by narrowing, not adding): in spec:159, spec:195 and spec:196 name the exact P1 set that gains the section (analyze, build, business-panel, design, document, explain, index, test), and say load changes its usage line only and the three small-fix ready commands change no flags. Priority High. Quality impact: consistency +1, testability +0.5.

findings.heading: ### F-1 [CRITICAL, blocking] Phase 1 gives 36 commands the `--unattended` flag but only 14 get their gate and outward-action rules there
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers (lead), Adzic (scenario), Whittaker (sequence attack). Priority: High. Quality impact: Consistency -2, safety boundary.
- Locations: `SPEC:159` (P1 row), `SPEC:195` (AC-1.1), `SPEC:154` and `SPEC:225` (Phases 1-3 need no user decision), `SPEC:60` (WC-2), `SPEC:67` (WC-9), `SPEC:100`, `SPEC:113`, `SPEC:114`, `SPEC:109` (rows assigned to P2 and P4), `SPEC:240` (D3 recommendation), `SPEC:73` (the brief always passes `--unattended`).
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows section 6 P1 and AC-1.1 as written gives every command in 3.1 and 3.2 except `/sc:load` the `--unattended` flag and the `## Unattended mode` section in Phase 1, while the rows for auggie-review, cleanup, task, post-release, pr-submit, implement and 15 others schedule their gate and outward-action resolutions for P2 to P4; that is wrong because WC-2 and WC-9 define `--unattended` as "never blocks on a person" and "every outward default is off", so a coordinator that follows `SPEC:73` and passes `--unattended` after P1 gets a command that still posts or still waits.
- Scenario (Adzic, with state trace):
  - Given P1 is complete, so AC-1.1 passes and `/sc:auggie-review` accepts `--unattended`, with the `--no-post-pr` implication still a P2 item (`SPEC:100`).
  - When the coordinator briefs `/sc:auggie-review 123 --unattended --output-dir D` (`SPEC:73`).
  - Then the command still posts `gh pr review --comment` plus inline comments with "No confirmation prompt" (`INV-A:38`), which `SPEC:67` says must be off. Before: 0 comments on the PR. After: review and inline comments posted.
  - Same trace for `/sc:post-release <v> --unattended` (VM, install, commit and PR confirmations remain, `INV-B:79,84`) and for `/sc:pr-submit --unattended`, which D3(a) (`SPEC:240`, "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4") may leave as a coordinator-only command, yet P1 has already changed it.
- Quantity check (FR-19): 36 commands flagged after P1, 14 behaviour-complete (8 no-gate P1 commands, 4 ready commands with P1 fixes, brainstorm, init-lite), 22 pending (15 P2, 4 P3, 3 P4). See the diagram below.
- Why the other reading does not rescue it: if "P1 writes each section with its full gate rules", the P2, P3 and P4 columns of `SPEC:97-125` and the claim that Phase 4 waits for D2-D4 (`SPEC:154`) no longer describe anything.
- Recommendation (narrow, no new rule): make the P1 scope and AC-1.1 match the rows. A command accepts `--unattended` and gets its section in the phase named in its own row (3.1 rows: P1 for the 10, with the P2 fixes landing in P2; 3.2 rows: the Phase column). Rationale: the flag then never exists without the behaviour WC-2 and WC-9 promise, and pr-submit, post-release and implement stay untouched until D2-D4 are answered.
